title: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component
abstract: arXiv:2611.28598v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Cylindrical data pair a vector in R^d with a direction in S^(m-1). We study a family in which the direction is von Mises-Fisher and, given the direction, the vector is Gaussian with mean affine in it; this generalizes the Mardia-Sutton model. The family is a curved exponential family inside a regular family with Fisher-Bingham directions. We state necessary and sufficient conditions for the maximum-likelihood estimator to exist and be unique. The estimator is explicit except for one scalar root and is the m-projection (Kullback-Leibler projection) of the moment-matching member. Every moment it does not match is a function of one residual, the gap between the sample and fitted second moments of the direction. The squared length of this gap in the Fisher metric is the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions, due to Cox on the circle and extended by Mardia, Holmes and Kent. translated_title: 圆柱分布的弯曲指数族：m-投影、曲率与von Mises-Fisher分量的检验
translated_abstract: 圆柱型数据由 R^d 中的一个向量与 S^(m-1) 上的一个方向配对组成。我们研究了一族分布，其中方向服从 von Mises-Fisher 分布，而在给定方向的条件下，向量服从高斯分布且其均值是方向的仿射函数；这推广了 Mardia-Sutton 模型。该分布族是具有 Fisher-Bingham 方向的正规分布族内部的一个弯曲指数族。我们给出了极大似然估计量存在且唯一的充分必要条件。该估计量除需求解一个标量方程的根之外均为显式表达式，并且它是矩匹配成员的 m-投影（即 Kullback-Leibler 投影）。该估计量未能匹配的每个矩都可以表示为单一残差的函数——即方向二阶矩的样本值与拟合值之间的差距。该差距在 Fisher 度量下的平方长度正是经典的 von Mises-Fisher 对 Fisher-Bingham 方向的得分检验，该检验源于 Cox 在圆上的工作，并由 Mardia、Holmes 和 Kent 加以推广。
tldr: 本文研究推广 Mardia-Sutton 模型的圆柱数据弯曲指数族，给出了极大似然估计存在唯一的充要条件及其作为 m-投影的显式构造，并证明该估计残差在 Fisher 度量下的平方长度恰为经典的 von Mises-Fisher 对 Fisher-Bingham 方向的得分检验。
en_tdlr: This paper studies a curved exponential family of cylindrical data generalizing the Mardia-Sutton model, establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for MLE existence and uniqueness, shows the estimator is an explicit m-projection up to one scalar root, and identifies the squared Fisher-metric length of the second-moment residual as the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions.
